newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RESEARCH ALERT-No slowdown seen in Malaysia Q3 GDP.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-No slowdown seen in Malaysia Q3 GDP.

text.p: Malaysia's third quarter economic growth would have remained strong at 8.4 percent, if not for an unpublicised upward revision of data for the same quarter a year ago, W.I. Carr said on Monday.

In a research note, the stockbrokerage said Bank Negara's report of a slower 8.0 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the third quarter, was helped by raising 1995's third quarter expansion to 9.3 percent from 8.9.
"If the 3Q95 figure was not revised up, the third quarter (1996) GDP growth would have been 8.4 percent, the same rate as the second quarter.
"In other words, there was no moderation on overall economic activity," W.I. Carr senior economist Dilip Ratha said in the note.
"This is in line with our view that growth is unlikely to slow down below 8.4 percent in 1996 as well as 1997, even though the authorities have forecast 8.2 percent growth (in 1996)," the note added.
Bank Negara raised the 1995 third quarter GDP growth to 9.3 percent after revising construction sector growth during that period to 20.9 percent from 14.1.
The Finance Ministry in its latest Economic Report projected that GDP growth will be at 8.2 percent this year and will slow further to 8.0 next year.
The economy expanded by 9.5 percent for the whole of last year, causing investor concern that the economy was overheating.
